title: What is a relying party intermediary under eIDAS 2.0?
summary: A relying party intermediary connects other organisations to the EUDI Wallet. Who registers, who holds which certificates and what stays with you.
body_markdown:
*Who registers, who holds the certificates and what an intermediary can take over.*


A relying party intermediary is an entity that is itself a registered relying party and gives other organisations access to its connection to the European Digital Identity Wallet. The intermediary takes over the integration and the communication with the wallet, and it can assist with the application for registration. The obligation to register, however, remains with the relying party. Authologic will act as an intermediary once it is entered in the register, after the national registers officially open.


The rules on intermediation are set at EU level, while the registers and procedures are national. The terms used in this article are defined in the[Digital Identity Glossary](https://authologic.com/blog/digital-identity-glossary-index) .
